summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for suprapubic pain and weakness related to an indwelling urinary catheter. He had presented to the ED multiple times in the prior week with catheter-related concerns. Evaluation revealed a urinary tract infection with Enterococcus on urine culture, localized suprapubic tenderness, and balanitis. He was started on ampicillin for the infection and oxybutynin for bladder spasms. His pain improved with medication, and his anxiety-related tremors resolved with supportive care and a single dose of Ativan. He was managed conservatively with no surgical intervention. Urology recommended daily hygiene, laxatives for bowel management, and follow-up. He was discharged home with services on hospital day 3 with resolved symptoms and clear instructions for antibiotic completion, hygiene, and follow-up.
